question:
An astronomical telescope is used by an observer in normal adjustment (final image at infinity). The objective is a circular aperture of diameter $D=10\,\text{cm}$ with focal length $f_o=100\,\text{cm}$, and the eyepiece has focal length $f_e=5\,\text{cm}$. The telescope is used to observe two distant stars emitting light of wavelength $\lambda=550\,\text{nm}$.

Assume the telescope is free from aberrations and the resolution is limited only by 

(i) diffraction at the objective (Rayleigh criterion) 

(ii) the resolving limit of the eye. The observer’s unaided eye can just resolve two point objects if they subtend an angle of at least $\alpha_0=3.0\times 10^{-4}\,\text{rad}$ at the eye.

Find the minimum angular separation $\Delta\theta_{\min}$ between the stars (in object space) so that the observer can just resolve them through this telescope.
